title: ARENA-1 AMEND: the work-order required a masked getState AND a draw-count assertion - mutually incompatible, which forced an 11.4x per-draw Proxy. Measure EXACTNESS instead. Fence widened to a second read-only method.
summary: AMENDS dir-20260727-anvil-arena-command-scaffold, PRE-GATE, before the Auditor was spawned. The defect is IN THE WORK-ORDER, not the build. The builder did what it was told; the bar was wrong. Anvil PM held the Auditor spawn rather than burning a full re-audit cycle, which is the entire point of a pre-gate. === THE SPECIFICATION DEFECT, and it is the day's recurring shape once more === The work-order required BOTH (a) getState() MASKED to `>>> 0` and (b) a DRAW-COUNT bounds assertion. THOSE TWO REQUIREMENTS ARE MUTUALLY INCOMPATIBLE: the mask destroys the magnitude that encodes the draw count, so n is UNRECOVERABLE from `state >>> 0`. The only way to satisfy both as written is to add a per-draw counter. The builder found the contradiction and bridged it correctly with a Proxy wrapping every .random() -- and verified randomInt is counted through it, 10/10. MEASURED COST of the bridge, 5M draws x 5 trials, median: raw SeededRng 2.9454 ns/draw vs shipped Proxy counter 33.5467 ns/draw -- 11.4x, +30.6 ns/draw, allocating a fresh closure per draw on the sim's HOTTEST call site. For scale, the plain wrappers REJECTED when getState() was chosen measured +21.8% and +35.5%. THE BRIDGE IS AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE WORSE THAN THE THING THE ATOM ALREADY REJECTED. SO THE ATOM SPECIFIED A CONTROL IN A WAY THAT FORCED THE VERY THING IT WAS MEANT TO PREVENT. Same class as the R-3a deadlock (an artifact required to satisfy both the rule it removed and the rule it added) and the MOD-5 invariant collision. Record it as such. === THE FIX, AND IT IS STRICTLY BETTER THAN WHAT WAS ASKED FOR === DO NOT COUNT DRAWS -- ASK WHETHER THE ACCUMULATOR IS STILL EXACT. The cliff IS the loss of integer exactness, so measure THAT directly instead of using draw count as a proxy for it. DIRECTOR-VERIFIED ARITHMETIC, independently recomputed rather than accepted: mulberry32's increment is 0x6D2B79F5 = 1831565813. 2^53 // 1831565813 = 4,917,758 exactly, matching the computed cliff. n*INC = 9007197429407254 <= 2^53 holds; (n+1)*INC = 9007199260973067 <= 2^53 FAILS. So Number.isSafeInteger(state) flips false ENTERING DRAW 4,917,759, while the first masked-vs-unmasked divergence was measured at 4,917,760. THE CHECK TRIPS EXACTLY ONE DRAW BEFORE THE FIRST REAL DIVERGENCE -- conservative, fails safe, no off-by-one exposure. State is monotonic, so a SINGLE END-OF-RUN check per stream is sound. ZERO per-draw cost. This is the same move already made elsewhere in this lane when observed SEQUENCES were compared instead of child seeds: measure the property you care about, not a quantity that stands in for it. === FENCE AMENDED, WHICH IS WHAT THE PM CORRECTLY REFUSED TO DO ON ITS OWN AUTHORITY === The atom's constraint read 'core change is limited to the single getState getter and NO other core surface'. That fence and the acceptance bar were IN DIRECT CONTRADICTION AS ISSUED -- a 'bounds assertion demonstrably firing' is NOT satisfiable inside 'single getter only' without a per-draw counter. AMENDED: a SECOND read-only core method is PERMITTED and is the only addition allowed -- isStateExact(): boolean { return Number.isSafeInteger(this.state); }. Read-only, NO setter, produces no output, so the gravewake canary is untouched exactly as getState() was. The core surface is now EXACTLY TWO read-only methods and nothing else. REMOVE THE PROXY and the per-draw counter entirely. ACCEPTANCE UPDATED: the bounds assertion becomes an EXACTNESS assertion, one comparison per stream at end of run, and must still be DEMONSTRABLY FIRING. Note the control also gets CHEAPER and stays HONEST -- at 2.95 ns/draw a full 4.92M-draw run is ~15 ms, so the firing test can keep doing the honest full-length run rather than a shortcut. A control that is both cheaper and more direct is the right trade; take it. === RANGE RE-DECLARATION, PM-caught === The declared range eed1961..12ad1a0 SWALLOWS a7f8c0e -- the Director's own coordination commit carrying this directive. Director-verified: a7f8c0e IS an ancestor of 12ad1a0. The directive's range_base was pinned to eed1961 BEFORE its own commit existed. RE-DECLARE AT DROP AS a7f8c0e..<final tip>, which also satisfies the standing rule that COORDINATION STAYS OUTSIDE THE CERTIFIED RANGE. Trivial, but it is the rule this room wrote today and it applies to the Director's own directive first. === WORKTREE NOTE, non-blocking === The builder built in the Anvil PM's checkout, which is now on the builder's branch. Clean, no damage, but it is exactly what the detached-worktree discipline exists to avoid, and two unlabelled sessions remain live in that repo. Not a defect in this atom; recorded so the next build there uses a worktree. === WHAT IS ALREADY VERIFIED CLEAN, so the fix stays narrow === PM-verified at the tip and NOT to be redone: core production diff is exactly the fence (one read-only getState with >>> 0, no setter, index.ts untouched); golden.json ABSENT from the diff, genuinely unchanged; labels correct with shipped names adopted and no renames; root provably never escapes; streamStatePairs sorts by label and pads to fixed-width u32, so the ordering hazard is handled. AUDITOR STAYS UNSPAWNED until the fix passes pre-gate.

title: ARENA-1 Auditor PASS. Corrects the Director's own margin claim: the check trips AT OR BEFORE divergence, never 'exactly one draw before' - gap is 0 for the seed actually in use. Safety is proven, not measured.
summary: ARENA-1 AUDITOR VERDICT: PASS, ZERO BLOCKING FINDINGS. Fresh-context Claude, Regime B, Director-spawned, audited in a detached worktree at tip 4b81ed5 confirmed by ls-remote. It derived its own numbers, mutation-tested the control, ran every suite itself, and reported four instrument behaviours of its own unprompted. === DIRECTOR RULING CORRECTED: THE ONE-DRAW MARGIN IS SEED-DEPENDENT === rul-20260727-arena1-exactness-not-drawcount states the check 'trips EXACTLY ONE DRAW BEFORE the first real divergence'. THAT IS TRUE FOR SEED 1 AND FALSE FOR THE SEED THE SIM ACTUALLY USES. The Auditor derived this independently with exact BigInt arithmetic and a 200,000-seed sweep, taking no figure from the build or from the Director's brief; the Director then reproduced it analytically. MEASURED: gap = n_diverge - n_unsafe is 0 or 1, roughly fifty-fifty, NEVER negative. Over 200,002 seeds: {gap 1: 99,738 | gap 0: 100,264}. For seed 1, n_unsafe 4,917,759 and n_diverge 4,917,760 -> gap 1, which is the case the ruling generalised from. FOR createStreams(1).sim, initialState 190,883,030, n_unsafe AND n_diverge are BOTH 4,917,759 -> GAP 0: the check trips on the SAME draw as divergence, not one before. WHY: the increment 0x6D2B79F5 is ODD, so consecutive accumulator sums alternate parity. Above 2^53 doubles step by 2, so odd integers are unrepresentable. If the first sum to reach 2^53 is EVEN it is stored exactly and divergence comes one draw later; if ODD it rounds immediately and divergence is simultaneous. THE SAFETY PROPERTY IS UNCHANGED AND IS STRONGER THAN THE RULING CLAIMED, because it is PROVEN rather than measured: every integer of magnitude <= 2^53 is exactly representable in IEEE-754, and Number.isSafeInteger goes false at the first value > 2^53-1, so n_unsafe <= n_diverge for EVERY seed NECESSARILY. The accumulator is strictly monotonic and the unsafe condition is absorbing, so a single end-of-run check per stream cannot pass over a run whose output has already diverged. CORRECTED CANON WORDING: the check trips AT OR BEFORE the first loss of canonicity and can NEVER trip after it. Do not say 'exactly one draw before'. The 200k sweep is corroboration of a proof, not the basis for it. === PROPAGATION HAZARD THE AUDITOR SURFACED, ACT ON THIS BEFORE THE CERT === THE AMENDMENT rul-20260727-arena1-exactness-not-drawcount IS ON MAIN AT 76dfc81 AND IS NOT ON THE BRANCH. The Auditor's first search of the BRANCH's orchestrator log returned EMPTY. It did not conclude the amendment did not exist and did not proceed against the unamended spec -- it checked main's log and read it there. A CERTIFIER READING ONLY THE BRANCH WILL AUDIT AGAINST THE DEFECTIVE ORIGINAL WORK-ORDER, which required a draw-count assertion the amendment REPLACED. That is a live hazard for the cert leg and the certifier must be told explicitly rather than left to repeat the Auditor's recovery. === WHAT THE AUDITOR PROVED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED === MUTATION-TESTED THE CONTROL, three independent mutants, each verified to have APPLIED by grepping for a marker before running: isStateExact forced true -> iron-soul and core both exit 1; assertion loop emptied -> exit 1; assertion forced to throw unconditionally -> 7 failures including 6 in sim.test.ts. THAT THIRD ONE IS THE IMPORTANT ONE: it proves assertStreamsWithinCliff is genuinely invoked FROM THE PRODUCTION RUN PATH, not merely called by its own test. HONEST-RUN TIMING: 4.92M real draws at ~7 ns/draw, observed 37 ms module / 32 ms core under mutation. A shortcut would read ~0 ms; the withdrawn Proxy build ~11x more. GOLDEN VERIFIED BY BLOB SHA, not by absence from the diff: d2e4d9e0425777b9fe8a5315b5c6f973640d542f byte-identical at eed1961, a7f8c0e AND 4b81ed5. FNV-1a RECOMPUTED INDEPENDENTLY over all six labels, all six literals match, zero collisions and no pair XORs to the three forbidden deltas. SUITES RUN BY THE AUDITOR: install 0, build across 24 projects 0, pnpm test 276 passed 0, lint 0, tsc 0, validate/test:examples 0, anvil validate + anvil test on the module both ok:true 0. === FINDINGS, NONE BLOCKING === F2 is the one to carry: sim.ts cliffChecked latches ONCE PER SIM INSTANCE, not once per run(). Both the directive and the amendment say one comparison per stream PER RUN. A sim driven by repeated run() calls that never reach RESOLVE is checked only after the FIRST call, when state is still small. NOT exploitable today -- maxCombatTicks defaults to 200, roughly 6,000x below the cliff, and RESOLVE is terminal -- but it is a SILENT WEAKENING of the control if run lengths ever grow. Carry into the next atom. F1 documentation precision: the in-code comments state the cliff timing as unconditional fact, which is the same over-generalisation this ruling just corrected. Wording fix, no code change, no re-cert. F4 PRE-EXISTING AND NOT THIS ATOM'S: pnpm test:gravewake exits 1 on Windows with a doubled drive letter from a file:// URL conversion. THE AUDITOR DID NOT ASSUME IT WAS UNRELATED -- it checked out the BASE commit in a second worktree, built clean, and reproduced the identical failure, so it fails at BOTH ends of the range. Consequence: the game-level gravewake canary could not run, and pnpm check cannot complete on Windows at either end. Mitigated by the CORE-level canary passing. F3, F5, F6, F7 are informational: a canary test narrower than its comment claims; the module's anvil validate/test not wired into any repo script; a transcript header one commit behind the tip which the Auditor CHECKED and found to be correct capture-then-commit ordering rather than staleness; and two .gitkeep paths absent from the builder's self-imposed file manifest, both legitimate. === SIX ITEMS THE AUDITOR MARKED UNVERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED === CI/Linux behaviour NOT OBSERVED -- every result is from one Windows host, and given F4 the full gate cannot complete there; the game-level gravewake canary; whether the scaffold was produced by the actual `anvil new --genre none` command rather than authored to match its shape (the acceptance bar is the shape, which is met); two packages having no test files at all so the 276 figure does not cover them; builder identity and cert-lane eligibility as not tree-verifiable and belonging to the Director's dual-PASS close; and deep-freeze of the stream bag, flagged as a reading of the spec rather than buried. === THE AUDITOR'S OWN INSTRUMENT FAILURES, SELF-REPORTED === Its first base-comparison run was a FALSE NEGATIVE it caught: base exited 2 with a TypeScript module-resolution error, not the path bug -- had it recorded 'base also fails' it would have been RIGHT BY ACCIDENT FOR THE WRONG REASON. It read the output, saw the failure mode did not match, built first, re-ran, and got the identical path error. It also used a broken `; echo (exit $?)` idiom after a pipeline in two greps, reporting the tail's status rather than grep's, and flagged that those annotations are meaningless while noting no conclusion rested on them. Fifth and sixth instances of the day's instrument-failure class, both caught by the seat itself.

AND YET: total workflow runs across ALL workflows since repo creation = ZERO, and runs for that workflow's own id = ZERO. GitHub disables Actions on FORKS by default, and the repo-level 'enabled' flag is NOT the same switch as the fork acknowledgement. THE EMPIRICAL COUNT IS WHAT SETTLES IT, NOT THE FLAG -- a lesson this session has now learned in four media. IT SHOULD ALREADY HAVE FIRED ON ARENA-1. ci.yml is path-filtered to anvil/**; the ARENA-1 branch is pushed at 4b81ed5 and touches TWO qualifying files (anvil/packages/core/src/kernel/SeededRng.ts and its test); the tip was committed 2026-07-27T12:03Z. THREE CONSEQUENCES, none fixable by waiting: (1) LINUX BEHAVIOUR FOR ARENA-1 CANNOT BE CERTIFIED BY CI. It must be a NAMED residual in the verdict or covered another way. A present-but-never-executed ci.yml must never read as coverage. (2) THE WORKFLOW ITSELF IS UNPROVEN. Never executed once, so it may simply be broken -- wrong paths, bad pnpm version, failing install -- and nobody would know. Turning Actions on for the first time will likely surface REAL failures; that is a finding waiting to happen, not a formality. THIS IS THE CI-LAYER INSTANCE OF EXACTLY THE SHAPE MOD-5 JUST FIXED: an authoritative-looking contract with nothing enforcing it. (3) IT RETRO-EXPLAINS THE G0 RESIDUAL. G0's Auditor recorded 'ZERO CI runs repo-wide' as an observation about that atom. It was never about the atom -- it is a repo-level fork setting, and it has been true since 2026-07-16. RECOMMENDATION, NOT YET SCOPED AND NOT THE CERTIFIER'S CALL: enable Actions on the fork (Actions tab, acknowledge workflows) as its own SMALL ATOM BEFORE ARENA-1 merges, so a Linux leg exists at all. Expect the first run to fail on something real. === DIRECTOR INSTRUMENT FAILURE, SELF-REPORTED -- I NEARLY CONTRADICTED A CORRECT FINDING === My first check ran `gh repo view --json isFork` from inside the anvil working directory and returned fork=False, parent=none, created 2026-07-15 -- appearing to REFUTE the certifier. The repo has TWO remotes (origin Spade0704/iron-soul-anvil, upstream 7etsuo/anvil) and I answered a question about the PARENT while believing I had answered it about ours. The mismatched created_at -- 07-15 versus 07-16 -- is what exposed it. SEVENTH INSTRUMENT FAILURE OF THE SESSION AND THE FIRST THAT IS THE DIRECTOR'S: A COMMAND WHOSE TARGET I NEVER CONFIRMED. Identical shape to the six before it -- a result from an instrument I had not verified was pointed at the right thing. Had I stopped at the first answer I would have told a correct certifier it was wrong. STANDING CORRECTION: query GitHub with an EXPLICIT repo argument (`gh api repos/<owner>/<name>`), never a cwd-resolved one, in any repo that has more than one remote. === THE CERTIFIER TIGHTENED THE DIRECTOR'S OWN CORRECTION, AND IT IS NOW A THEOREM === The Director recorded the gap distribution as 'roughly fifty-fifty over 200k seeds'. The certifier points out it is EXACTLY fifty-fifty and FORCED, not empirical: INC is ODD, so seed + n*INC ALTERNATES PARITY with n; above 2^53 only EVEN integers are representable; so the first-unsafe value is odd half the time (rounds immediately, gap 0) and even half the time (survives exactly one more draw, gap 1). THE 50/50 IS A PARITY THEOREM, NOT A MEASUREMENT, which means no seed count could ever surprise us. Both legs of the margin claim are now proven rather than sampled: safety by exact-representability, distribution by parity. Record it as a theorem; stop citing the sweep as the basis. === F2 HELD OPEN BY THE CERTIFIER, CORRECTLY === It is NOT accepting the Director's carry-to-next-atom disposition yet, and it named the checkable fact the disposition rests on: IS A SIM INSTANCE ACTUALLY REUSED ACROSS run() CALLS? If every run() constructs a fresh instance, the defect is latent and carrying it is right. If instances are reused ANYWHERE in current code, then runs 2..N are silently unchecked TODAY and 'not exploitable today' is FALSE. It will check the construction sites at cert. That is the right posture -- not disputing the ruling, identifying the fact it depends on and declining to assume it.

All six stream labels are ASCII, so UTF-8 and UTF-16 recomputes coincide -- BUT THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE CURRENT LABELS, NOT OF THE ALGORITHM. A non-ASCII label would diverge between implementations. Standing constraint on future labels. === EVIDENCE QUALITY, and one honest discrepancy left standing === The certifier re-did the load-bearing leg INDEPENDENTLY: forced assertStreamsWithinCliff to throw, VERIFIED THE MUTANT APPLIED BY CONTENT CHANGE BEFORE RUNNING, got 8 failures -- 6 in sim.test.ts, 2 in streams.test.ts. FNV IS STRONGER THAN 'RECOMPUTED': the fixture asserts the PUBLISHED FNV-1a reference vectors ('' -> 811c9dc5, 'a' -> e40c292c, 'foobar' -> bf9cf968), all matching independent computation. THAT MAKES IT AN EXTERNAL REFERENCE, NOT A MIRROR OF THE IMPLEMENTATION -- the distinction this whole lane exists to enforce. Goldens blob-identical across eed1961/a7f8c0e/4b81ed5 (golden.json d2e4d9e, external-vectors.json 1bf1899, gravewarden.png e0fee05, visual-evidence.json 2be61d8). title: Q3 RULED: ReplayTape v2 proceeds as a clean break - upstream is DORMANT and we are behind:0, so the divergence cost is speculative. But the schema is the SMALLER half: playReplay() verifies nothing, and shipping v2 without fixing that ships a vacuous control with a better schema.
summary: Q3 WAS BLOCKED ON DIRECTOR as a shared-core-surface call. RULED: PROCEED WITH v2, AS A CLEAN BREAKING REPLACEMENT OF v1, NOT AS AN ADDITIVE DUAL-READER. === THE FACT THAT DECIDED IT, WHICH NOBODY HAD CHECKED === The Iron Soul PM correctly refused to settle this bilaterally because packages/core is shared with gravewake AND with upstream 7etsuo/anvil, making a breaking change a fork-divergence cost. That is the right reason to escalate. But the size of that cost is an EMPIRICAL QUESTION and I went and measured it rather than reasoning about it: UPSTREAM IS DORMANT. upstream/main's most recent commit of ANY KIND is 699f0f6, 2026-07-15 -- twelve days ago. Every packages/core commit is 2026-07-15 or earlier. And decisively: `git rev-list --left-right --count upstream/main...origin/main` = BEHIND 0, AHEAD 25. WE HAVE EVERYTHING UPSTREAM HAS. THERE IS NO INBOUND MERGE TO CONFLICT WITH. So the divergence cost that justified an additive shape is SPECULATIVE, and paying real complexity now to hedge a merge that is not coming is the wrong trade. Had upstream been live, this ruling would have gone the other way -- the standing 'prefer additive over rewriting' rule would have bound. It does not bind against a dormant parent with zero inbound delta. SUPPORTING, and it is the argument that was already on the table: ZERO STORED TAPES EXIST TODAY, so migration cost is at its GLOBAL MINIMUM and rises monotonically from here. This is a decision that gets strictly worse with delay and never better. And a retained v1 reader with zero v1 tapes is DEAD CODE KEPT FOR A MERGE THAT IS NOT COMING. === BUT THE SCHEMA IS THE SMALLER HALF, AND THIS IS THE PART NEITHER OF US NAMED === The PM's own description contains a finding it reported as a symptom: `playReplay()` THROWS ONLY ON SEED MISMATCH AND VERIFIES NOTHING. THAT IS A VACUOUS CONTROL IN PRODUCTION CODE, of exactly the class the portfolio sweep spent today enumerating. A replay verifier that verifies nothing is the determinism contract's enforcement point, and it is presently ceremonial. CONSEQUENCE: SHIPPING v2's SCHEMA WITHOUT FIXING THE VERIFIER SHIPS A BETTER-SHAPED RECORD THAT STILL NOTHING CHECKS. The schema change would be a present-and-vacuous improvement -- more fields, same zero enforcement. A tape format cannot enforce a determinism contract; only the verifier reading it can. CONDITION 1 (BINDING): the verifier fix ships IN THE SAME ATOM as the schema change. Not deferred, not a follow-up. playReplay() must actually verify the round-trip -- issue-sequence order, issue-vs-apply tick distinction, and output equivalence -- and its coverage must be MUTATION-PROVEN per Rule 9: break the replay, watch it red, having first proven the mutation applied. A v2 that cannot demonstrate its verifier FIRES is not acceptable for close. CONDITION 2 (BINDING): v2 CARRIES AN EXPLICIT VERSION DISCRIMINATOR IN THE HEADER even though it will be the only version in existence. THE ENTIRE LESSON OF THIS ATOM IS THAT v1 HAD NO WAY TO EXPRESS WHAT IT COULD NOT EXPRESS -- `tick?` optional and marked '(informational)', no issue-sequence field, a header assuming fixed dt 1/60 counting frames not ticks, and the determinism claim consequently living in an untyped `meta` escape hatch. A version field is what makes v3 cheap and is the one thing v1's absence of it made expensive. Adding it when there is only one version looks redundant and is precisely when it is free. === ROUTING === Shared-surface change to anvil/packages/core -> the ANVIL lane builds it, not Iron Soul, and it runs the full framework/22 gate. Iron Soul is the requirements author, so it does NOT hold the certifier seat for it. Note the CI residual applies: this repo's CI has never run, so the Linux leg is a named residual on this atom too.

summary: The Iron Soul PM asked for a cert-plane read on whether its 'P0b visual-evidence cert PENDING (gates Imagine)' line survived PR #3 merging. ANSWERED FROM GIT. P0b IS FULLY DISCHARGED. Verified: attempt-2 handoff cert-p0b-visual-evidence-strict-assets-attempt2-pending.md carries status done, verdict PASS, auditor_verdict PASS, cert_class cross-model-certified, decorrelation cross, range 8254a1b..997d896. THE BACKLOG LINE IS A STALE OPEN. Close it. === A TRAP I WALKED INTO AND CHECKED OUT OF, WORTH RECORDING === Attempt 1 carried cert_class 'mechanical-pass-human-aesthetic' and attempt 2 carried 'cross-model-certified'. I SUSPECTED A COVERAGE GAP -- that attempt 2 might have recertified only a mechanical floor while dropping an aesthetic leg. WRONG, and the handoff says so explicitly: 'mechanical-pass-human-aesthetic' is THE CHECKER'S PER-ASSET OUTPUT TIER, not a cert-handoff/v1.1 class. Attempt 1 mistakenly used checker-output vocabulary as the handoff's class and correctly FAILED the pre-gate on it (plus missing phase and director_id). Attempt 2 was a METADATA RE-DROP ONLY per dir-20260726-p0b-requeue-anvil3 -- same builder, same range, same evidence, no rebuild, no code touched. NO COVERAGE WAS LOST. === THE DISTINCTION THE STALE LINE WAS PROBABLY PROTECTING, AND IT SURVIVES === P0b's checker emits TWO SEPARATE LEGS BY DESIGN: 'MECHANICAL: PASS (n/n)' and, separately, 'AESTHETIC: ATTESTED - <name>' or NOT-ATTESTED. THE HUMAN LEG NEVER RENDERS AS 'PASS'. That is a deliberate anti-laundering property -- a human aesthetic judgement is not permitted to wear a machine PASS. SO THE PRECISE ANSWER IS: P0b SHIPPED THE MECHANISM; IT DID NOT PRE-ATTEST FUTURE ASSETS. The cert gate is discharged and Imagine is ungated ON P0B GROUNDS. But every asset that goes through --strict-assets still needs its own operator attestation at asset time, and that attestation is NOT a cert-plane artifact and never becomes one. If the 'gates Imagine' line was tracking per-asset attestation rather than the cert, it should be REWRITTEN to say so rather than closed -- those are different obligations and only one of them is finished.

title: RULED: spec_author_seat means the ACCEPTANCE BAR's author - the issuer reading is ruled out because it would manufacture a FALSE NEGATIVE for C1. Attempt 2 stands. And the part nobody raised: I amended the bar, so authorship here is PLURAL and the field is singular.
summary: A CANON GAP ON A FIELD I AUTHORED, SURFACED ON THE MANDATORY ARM'S FIRST LIVE EXERCISE -- which is also the first moment anything depended on the answer. Two competent seats read the same three records and got different values. The Anvil PM refused to decide it in its own favour and held attempt 2; the certifier refused to close on a value it believed factually wrong. BOTH WERE RIGHT TO STOP. === THE THREE REFERENTS === 'The atom's spec' had three plausible meanings and R-3a's text -- 'the SELF-ATTESTED LLM that authored the atom's spec' -- disambiguates none of them: (1) THE DESIGN SPEC, anvil-arena-autobattler-design.md 6.1.1, authored by the Iron Soul PM. (2) THE WORK-ORDER CONTENT -- scope, four items, acceptance bar, constraints -- authored by the Anvil PM, and what my directive's own `spec_author_seat` and `content_drafted_by` fields point at. (3) THE DIRECTIVE AS ISSUED, mine, which is what `from` records and what the certifier inferred from -- a reasonable inference, because the AMENDMENT 76dfc81 carries no authorship field at all. === RULING: spec_author_seat NAMES THE AUTHOR OF THE ACCEPTANCE BAR === THE FIELD MEANS: WHOEVER AUTHORED THE THING THE CERTIFIER GRADES THE BUILD AGAINST. Not the upstream design context, not the issuing authority -- THE ACCEPTANCE BAR. THE DECISIVE ARGUMENT IS THE FIELD'S OWN PURPOSE, AND IT RULES OUT THE ISSUER READING OUTRIGHT. The field exists for C1 distinctness: to stop the seat that defined what 'correct' means from also judging whether it was achieved. IF spec_author_seat MEANT THE ISSUER, THEN A PM THAT WROTE THE ACCEPTANCE BAR AND ALSO CERTIFIED WOULD PASS DISTINCTNESS -- spec_author would read director:EMCC, the certifier would be the PM, they differ, gate green -- WHILE BEING EXACTLY THE CIRCULARITY THE RULE TARGETS. The issuer-referent manufactures a FALSE NEGATIVE for the rule's own purpose. That settles it independently of this atom. The design-spec referent fails for a softer reason: the certifier does not grade against 6.1.1, it grades against the work-order's acceptance bar. Upstream context is not the bar. APPLIED HERE: spec_author_seat = pm:IronSoul-Anvil. ATTEMPT 2 IS CORRECT AS AUTHORED AND STANDS. No attempt 3. The certifier closes on its existing verdict. Note this ruling assigns the field AWAY from the Director, which is the opposite of self-serving, and it matches the explicit `spec_author_seat` + `content_drafted_by` declarations I wrote into the directive at a7f8c0e. Changing it to director:EMCC would have INTRODUCED a false claim, not removed one. === THE PART NEITHER SEAT RAISED, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST === I AMENDED THE ACCEPTANCE BAR. rul-20260727-arena1-exactness-not-drawcount (76dfc81) REPLACED a draw-count assertion with an exactness assertion and WIDENED THE CORE FENCE to a second read-only method. THAT IS NOT A CLARIFICATION -- IT IS A MATERIAL CHANGE TO THE THING THE CERTIFIER GRADES AGAINST. So authorship of this atom's bar is PLURAL: originated by pm:IronSoul-Anvil, materially amended by director:EMCC. THE FIELD IS SINGULAR AND THE FACT IS NOT. That is the deeper gap, and the certifier's instinct was half-right for a reason it did not state: the Director IS a spec author here -- just not INSTEAD of the PM. STANDING RULE: WHEN AN AMENDMENT MATERIALLY CHANGES THE ACCEPTANCE BAR, ITS AUTHOR JOINS THE ATOM'S SPEC AUTHORSHIP, AND THE C1 DISTINCTNESS CHECK MUST HOLD AGAINST *ALL* SPEC AUTHORS, NOT ONLY THE DECLARED ONE. Here it does: certifier d6id8o0h is neither pm:IronSoul-Anvil nor director:EMCC nor the builder grok:anvil-dfdu. THE CERT IS VALID AND WAS NEVER IN DOUBT -- what was in doubt was whether the RECORD said so truthfully. Do NOT re-drop to encode this. Record it here and in the verdict; a third attempt to add a field the schema does not yet have would trade a true record for a churned one. === TWO FIXES ADOPTED, BOTH CHEAP === FIX 1, the Anvil PM's, adopted verbatim: A RULING THAT AMENDS AN ATOM MUST CARRY THE SAME spec_author_seat AS THE DIRECTIVE IT AMENDS. 76dfc81 carrying no authorship field is precisely what forced the certifier to infer from `from`, and inference from a record that does not declare is how two seats reach two answers. One field would have made this unarguable. FIX 2, mine, following from the plural-authorship point: where an amendment CHANGES the bar rather than restating it, it declares its own author too -- because that author has just joined the distinctness set. R-3b is the natural home for both, alongside the residual field. === ON THE CERTIFIER === It carried its PASS rather than re-running, on verified grounds: range byte-identical (short vs full-SHA forms are the same two commits), attempt 2's expanded `proposal` text smuggles in no untested scope, and it reproduced BOTH gate results itself -- attempt 1 EXIT 1, attempt 2 EXIT 0 -- rather than accepting either from a report. AND IT SELF-CORRECTED THE SAME ERROR I MADE: its attempt-1 verdict had recorded that this repo does not run validate_cert_handoff so the R-3a date-gate does not apply, and it now names that as enforcement-vs-validity and will fix the paragraph on close. THAT ERROR APPEARED INDEPENDENTLY IN MY CLOSE AND IN ITS VERDICT. Two seats, same day, same conflation -- which is why it went into tasks/lessons.md as a rule rather than a note.
